name: Clockwise
tagline: Rearrange flexible holds around fixed meetings for one user's calendar

pricing.notes: Advertised annual-equivalent team price; monthly options may differ.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Clockwise, rearrange flexible holds around fixed meetings for one user's calendar. The hard boundary is organization-wide optimization, calendar graph, team adoption, and conflict safety, plus calendar integrations and reliability.
coreLoopDIY: Read one user's calendar, rearrange flexible holds around fixed meetings, create conflict-safe bookings, and send confirmations and reminders.
whatYouLose: organization-wide optimization, calendar graph, team adoption, and conflict safety
ongoingBurden: OAuth refresh, webhooks, timezone databases, race conditions, reminders, deliverability, privacy, and uptime
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Clockwise because people pay because one double booking or missed invite can cost more than years of subscription fees. The recurring cost buys OAuth refresh, webhooks, timezone databases, race conditions, reminders, deliverability, privacy, and uptime, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Cal.com
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source scheduling platform with calendar integrations and booking workflows.

alternatives.name: FlowSavvy Free
alternatives.desc: It auto-plans unlimited tasks for the next two weeks; priorities and dependencies are how the paid plan gets you.

facts.install: Create a hosted account in the web app or install the iOS or Android app
facts.engines: A deterministic scheduling algorithm; FlowSavvy explicitly says it does not use machine learning to build schedules
facts.dataFormat: Tasks, events, and settings live in FlowSavvy's cloud database and synchronize with connected Google, Outlook, or iCloud calendars; the service currently provides no general calendar import or export
facts.gapVsPaid: FlowSavvy optimizes one person’s tasks and events, not the team-wide meeting negotiation and shared focus-time coordination Clockwise provided before shutting down.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires an internet connection; calendar synchronization requires OAuth or app-specific credentials

alternatives.name: Reclaim Lite
alternatives.desc: The free solo plan moves focus, habits, breaks and meetings around; the planning horizon is one week.

alternatives.name: Trevor AI Free
alternatives.desc: One calendar gets task-to-time-block planning and some AI suggestions; multiple calendars and deeper automation cost extra.

facts.install: Create a hosted web account and connect one supported calendar; the web app can be installed to a home screen
facts.engines: A private per-user deep-learning scheduling model; some language features use OpenAI, according to Trevor's documentation
facts.dataFormat: Tasks, calendar events, and scheduling state are processed and stored in Trevor's hosted infrastructure, with connected calendar data synchronized through provider APIs
facts.gapVsPaid: Trevor schedules one person’s tasks around one calendar but does not optimize meetings and focus blocks across an organization as Clockwise did.
facts.setupBlocker: No native desktop or mobile app; calendar integrations require OAuth, and the free tier is limited to one calendar account

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Teams plan and a single-user booking service DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Clockwise in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, Google Calendar OAuth, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: read one user's calendar, rearrange flexible holds around fixed meetings, create conflict-safe bookings, and send confirmations and reminders.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement one account with configurable working hours, buffers, minimum notice, and booking horizon.
Connect Google Calendar using OAuth and store refresh tokens encrypted at rest.
Calculate availability in UTC and render it in the visitor's detected timezone.
Reserve slots transactionally, create calendar events, and prevent concurrent double booking.
Send confirmation, cancellation, and reminder email with signed management links.
Add an admin booking list, event-type editor, audit log, and calendar reconnect flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out Microsoft and Apple calendar support.
Deliberately leave out team round-robin routing.
Deliberately leave out payments, CRM workflows, and enterprise controls.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
discontinued: shut down on March 27, 2026 after the team joined Salesforce, with prepaid time refunded pro rata
